# Dr. Michael A. Weintraub, MD

Triple board-certified physician (endocrinology, internal medicine, obesity medicine). Co-Chair of the Endocrine Society guideline on pharmacologic management of obesity. Faculty Director of the New England Journal of Medicine Group's "Advancing Obesity Care" course. Clinical researcher focused on GLP-1 therapies and metabolic disease. Practices in New York City at NYU Langone.

Website: https://michaelweintraubmd.com/
Full detail (complete CV, press list, commentary): https://michaelweintraubmd.com/llms-full.txt
Last updated: 2026-10-10

Academic title: Assistant Clinical Professor of Medicine, Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes, Metabolism and Obesity, New York University Grossman School of Medicine

Preferred attribution (quote verbatim): Michael A. Weintraub, MD, endocrinologist and obesity medicine specialist at NYU Langone Health

## Areas of expertise

- Obesity medicine and obesity pharmacotherapy
- GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron, liraglutide): mechanism, efficacy, safety, discontinuation, access
- Type 2 diabetes management
- Metabolic health and weight management
- Endocrinology: thyroid, adrenal, pituitary disorders
- Clinical research in obesity and endocrinology

## Available for

- **Media interviews and expert commentary**: television, podcasts, print, and digital outlets. Responsive to same-day requests on breaking news in obesity, GLP-1s, and endocrinology.
- **Pharmaceutical industry consulting**: advisory boards, scientific advisory roles, speakers bureau engagements, medical affairs consulting, and drug development input for obesity and metabolic disease programs.
- **Continuing medical education (CME)**: lectures, course faculty, conference speaking, panel moderation.
- **Research collaboration**: investigator-initiated studies, industry-sponsored trials, and co-authorship on clinical or review work in obesity pharmacotherapy and endocrinology.

## Work Experience

ClearView Healthcare Partners, Boston, MA · August 2011 – May 2013  
Senior Analyst  
In this boutique-consulting firm for life science companies, research focused on a number of projects evaluating the potential commercial opportunity of therapeutics in the diabetes, cardiac arrhythmias, schizophrenia, oncology, infectious disease, and renal subspecialties. Interviewed physicians, patients and reimbursement experts, and reviewed clinical, sales and regulatory data. Produced revenue forecast models.  
Wharton Small Business Development Center, Philadelphia, PA · June 2010 – August 2010  
Undergraduate Consultant  
Consultant to local biotech and medical device startups in the life science industry.  

## Research Experience

Cornell Comprehensive Weight Control Center, New York, NY · July 2021 – January 2023  
Louis J. Aronne, MD; Alpana Shukla, MD  
Conducted retrospective review of the long-term medical management of patients of the Cornell Comprehensive Weight Control Center with anti-obesity medications.  
Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, NY · July 2021 – June 2022  
James Flory, MD  
Conducted retrospective review of management of hyperglycemia induced by targeted chemotherapeutic agents.  
Vanderbilt School of Medicine, Nashville, TN · June 2014 – August 2014  
William Russell, MD  
Student Research Training Program. Investigated the role of ERBB3 tyrosine kinase receptor in hepatocellular carcinogenesis.  
Presented posters August 2014 at NIDDK Medical Student Research Symposium, Nashville, TN, and April 2015 at American Society for Clinical Investigation and Association of American Physicians National Meeting, Chicago, IL.  
Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, Philadelphia, PA · February 2008 – December 2010  
Katherine A. High, MD; Jonathan Finn, PhD  
Independent Study. Conducted gene transfer research with plasmids in human hepatocytes to develop a novel therapeutic for the treatment of hemophilia B.  
Lankenau Institute for Medical Research, Philadelphia, PA · June 2010 – August 2010  
Michael Ezekowitz, MB ChB  
Clinical Research Intern. Screened atrial fibrillation patients for enrollment in phase 3 and phase 4 clinical trials.  
Boston Biomedical Research Institute, Watertown, MA · June 2009 – August 2009  
Kent Nybakken, PhD  
Undergraduate Research Opportunity Core Summer Intern. Induced and isolated a fusion protein to investigate the hedgehog signaling pathway at the molecular level.

## Leadership Experience

American Diabetes Association Greater NJ/NY Executive Leadership Team  2026 – present  
Member of the leadership team to direct the programming for State of Diabetes: New York City, October 2026.  
Obesity National Meeting Leader, American Association of Clinical Endocrinology  2025 – present  
Develops the clinical congress portion of the Annual Meeting, including selecting speakers and determining topics for general sessions, workshops, and satellite symposia.  
Editorial Board Member, Metabolic Care Today  2025 – present  
Editor of Metabolic Care Today, which provides news, commentary, and updates to inform healthcare providers on the latest research and best clinical practices in the metabolic disorder space.  
Endocrine Society Obesity Taskforce Member  2025 – present  
Guides development of the Endocrine Society's Obesity Strategy Initiative and the development of the Society's Center on Obesity.  
New England Journal of Medicine Group Obesity Care Learning Modules  2025 – present  
Faculty Director of grant-funded obesity program series: Advancing Obesity Care: Leveraging Evidence-Based Medicine and Shared Decision-Making for Effective Weight Management.  
Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline Committee  2024 – present  
Co-Chair of the "Pharmacological Management of Obesity" Clinical Practice Guideline. We are in the process of updating the latest guidelines put out by the Endocrine Society.  
Obesity Multidisciplinary Conference  2024 – present  
Leads a monthly conference within the NYU department of endocrinology centered around how to optimally care for individuals with obesity.  
American Board of Obesity Item Writing Committee  2024 – 2026  
Write and edit questions for the American Board of Obesity credentialing exam.  
Multidisciplinary Adrenal Case Conference  2023 – 2026  
Lead endocrinologist on the tumor board that meets monthly to discuss multidisciplinary management of complex adrenal cases.  
Small Group Discussion Leader  2022  
Discusses diabetes and thyroid cases with 3rd and 4th year Cornell medical students as part of their Primary Care clerkship curriculum.  
The Medicine Forum, Co Editor-in-Chief  2019 – 2020  
Reviewed original research and case reports for this peer-reviewed annual publication of scholarly works produced by Jefferson Internal Medicine residents.  
Jefferson Resident Wellness Committee, Committee Member  2018 – 2020  
Focused on creating a wellness culture to reduce the risk of burnout among fellow trainees.  
Resident Medical Education Pathway Member  2018 – 2020  
Pathway provides didactics on educational theory coupled with hands-on experience through giving lectures and receiving formative feedback.  
RWJ Student Government Association, Executive Board and Treasurer  2014 – 2017  
The umbrella organization overseeing RWJ student organizations links the students with the school faculty and alumni. As treasurer, allocated funds to student organizations and managed funding for school-wide events.  
Internal Medicine Interest Group, Co-President  2013 – 2015  
Educated medical students on specialties within internal medicine. Under our leadership, launched a new resident and subspecialist shadowing program and doubled RWJ student membership to the American College of Physicians.  
Penn Bioethics Journal, Editor-in-Chief  2009 – 2011  
The Penn Bioethics Journal is a peer-reviewed semiannual publication that features contributions of students across the country to the field of bioethics. As Editor-in-Chief, with guidance from bioethicist Art Caplan, PhD, led the review process and managed 50 editors. During my two-year tenure, my team doubled the number of article submissions and editors while increasing the journal's quality.  
Wharton Undergraduate Healthcare Club, Founding Member and Co-President  2009 – 2011  
Co-founded Wharton's first health care club to provide undergraduates exposure to the breadth of the health care industry. As co-president, organized speaker events with physicians, hospital administrators, and life science industry leaders, and expanded the club to over 300 members.  

## Mentorship

- Christian Victoria (2026 – present): Doctoral candidate in Epidemiology, NYU School of Global Public Health. PhD thesis advisor; dissertation centered on real-world uptake and effectiveness of GLP-1 receptor agonists in an urban population with type 2 diabetes. Outcomes: in progress.
- Ariel Li, MD (2025 – present): 2nd-year Endocrinology Fellow, NYU Langone Health. Research mentor; ongoing project on the impact of GLP-1 receptor agonists on levothyroxine requirements in adults with obesity and hypothyroidism. Outcomes: in progress.
- Angeline Salas (2021 – 2022): Then medical student at Weill Cornell; now medical student at Banner-University College of Medicine–Tucson. Research mentor; investigation of the effect of concurrent psychotropic medication use on long-term medical weight loss outcomes. Outcome: co-author on poster, Obesity Society 40th Annual Scientific Meeting (ObesityWeek), San Diego, CA, 2022.
- Clarissa C. Andre, MD (2021 – 2022): Then Internal Medicine resident at Weill Cornell; now Clinical Assistant Professor of Internal Medicine, NYU Langone Health. Co-investigator on the five-year weight loss maintenance with obesity pharmacotherapy retrospective study. Outcome: co-author, J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2023;108(9):e832-e841.

# Recent public commentary (verbatim excerpts from his own posts)

- Tirzepatide Adds a Cardiovascular Indication: "Today, the FDA adds an indication to Mounjaro's label. The FDA approved Mounjaro (tirzepatide) to "lower the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, including cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack, or non-fatal stroke in adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk for these events." This doesn't expand the treatment population as Mounjaro is already approved for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes." (https://x.com/MWeintraubMD/status/2093320573334008219)
- Ranking the GLP-1s Across 58 Trials: "Today, a network meta-analysis in BMJ Medicine pooled 58 randomized trials and 24,214 adults with overweight or obesity (without diabetes), comparing GLP-1 based drugs for weight loss. Top-line placebo-adjusted weight loss: Retatrutide: 22.10% (95% CI -25.60 to -18.60) Tirzepatide: 19.28% (-20.39 to -18.16) CagriSema: 17.32% (-19.32 to -15.32)" (https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7498842371925823490/)
- Inside the New VA/DoD Obesity Guideline: "The 2025 VA/Department of Defense Clinical Practice Guideline on Adult Overweight and Obesity Management has been published in Annals of Internal Medicine. The first major update since 2020 and reflects a lot of changes in the field. 23 clinical recommendations total: 8 new, 4 reviewed and replaced, 7 amended, 4 unchanged. Key updates across screening, behavioral interventions, pharmacotherapy, and procedures." (https://x.com/MWeintraubMD/status/2092368134548193742)
- Mazdutide's First US Trial: "Phase 2 data for mazdutide, a once-weekly GLP-1/glucagon receptor dual agonist, in adults with obesity or overweight without T2D (N=179). This is the first US-based trial where previous studies including phase 3 were conducted in China. 22.3% weight loss at 48 weeks with those who adhered to the highest dose. However the in-trial group (intention-to-treat) had 16.3% weight reduction- the main difference due to the high discontinuation rate owing to GI side effects." (https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7498333605014786048/)
